reviews.review:
I don't mind short games but I expect more than 35 minutes if I am paying for a story driven experience, even if the narrative is decently paced (which it is), you have to give me like 90 minutes so I have the time to appreciate the journey. You can travel between different memories of the character with walking-sim gameplay, so you should have utilized that to create more variety and navigational escapism -- the garden area and the library part were not bad, but I think the game needed at least another 3 dreamy locations like that.

The story was a little too simple for my taste, there are dozens of games on Steam that do exactly the same thing where the character is going through grief and collects their happy memories, and generally those games have more depth or context (at least those that are worth playing), where this game just leaves it at the surface level. I didn't really mind the actual delivery of the story, I think the voice actors did a good job conveying their emotions in the moment, but overall the experience is very basic, there are too many games that have a similar narrative and are more compelling.

There were a few puzzles, I pretty much solved all of them under 1 minute so they didn't add a lot to the gameplay, I think the use of a hint for the lock was clever, but the game needed more puzzles like that with more locations. The visuals were just okay for the price, I think the garden area looked pretty good, you had a decent amount of detail for the apartment, granted you only have a few areas, so maybe you could have done more interactions just to kill more time and provide more context for their problems. I had to switch to medium settings because it felt like the light effects were not properly optimized, I could feel them having an effect on the camera movement. 

[h1] Pros: [/h1]

(+) Fully voice acted, decently. The pacing of the narrative was not bad, if it was at a bit longer and maintained that pacing I think it would be a decent game

(+) The visuals/detail were okay for the price

[h1] Feedback: [/h1]

- 35 minutes is just too short, I think you should aim for a few hours for walking-sim games, it's a cheap game, but there are demos that are the same length. I think the areas like the garden and that book location were not bad, but I was expecting another 3 locations like that at the minimum

(On that note, it's always beneficial to add more optional interactions and more optional achievements, make the player want to explore and look at things)

- the narrative was a little too simple in my opinion, I think you will find many games on steam that do the exact same thing, but with more depth and context, with multiple hours of visuals. So, what it is about this game that makes it stand out or makes it any different than anything I played before? 

- it felt to me like the light effects on high settings were not optimized, but I can't speak for anyone else, I could feel it affecting the camera 

- check if the achievement is working, not sure what it was for but I didn't get it

[b] Overall Thoughts: 4/10 [/b]

I played so many great walking-sim games over the years that had a similar narrative, this felt like the exact same experience but much less in terms of context, not sure if it was like a learning project, but it's a little too simple, you need to come up with a more original narrative and settings. I think the voice acting was decent, the locations were not bad, but you should have more memories to explore, the game is just too short, and does not have anything new to offer that I have not experienced before in greater depth. I would recommend at least aiming for a few hours of exploration, maybe with more optional content or achievement hunting.
